documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT. 52M, runs a landscaping crew, here to set up primary care; his last office closed its internal medicine side over the summer and he has been coasting on refills.

Known problems per pt: high blood pressure for years, cholesterol, and a heart scan last year that showed some plaque in one artery. Saw cardiology once for that, told to keep the statin and the BP pill, no stents, nothing further. Denies exertional chest discomfort, dyspnea, palpitations, leg swelling. Gets winded hauling mulch bags up a slope at the end of a long day but no different from the rest of the crew.

Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily. Takes both, rarely misses.
Allergies: none to medicines.
PSH: none.
FH: dad had a heart attack at 62. Mom has blood pressure. One brother on a cholesterol pill.
SH: smokes a pack a day, started in his early 20s, so roughly 30 pack-years. A drink or two a month at a cookout. No other substances. Outdoors all season, plows in winter.

Exam: well-appearing, weathered. BP above, recheck similar. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd benign. No peripheral edema, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN on lisinopril 20: a bit above goal today. Home cuff readings requested before changing anything.
2. Hyperlipidemia / CAD (nonobstructive on 2021 CT angio per pt): continue atorvastatin 40. Lipids today. Records request to prior office for the CT report.
3. Tobacco: talked through what quitting would mean for the plaque already there. He is not ready, says the job and the smoking go together. Will keep asking.
4. Lung cancer screening: qualifies by age and pack-years. Low-dose CT ordered.
5. Health maintenance: colonoscopy around 2019 at old office, normal per pt. Hep C and HIV once, A1c screen, CMP, CBC today. Flu shot given.

RTC 6 months or sooner with home BP numbers.

The radiology department will call you to schedule the lung CT. Thanks.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — GENERAL SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/07/2024, discharged 05/13/2024.

Principal diagnosis: bleeding gastric ulcer, status post operative repair.
Secondary: acute hemolytic transfusion reaction.

Course: 54-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease and ongoing cigarette use brought in overnight after vomiting blood at home. In the ED he was pallid, sweaty and hypotensive; two large-bore lines were placed and crystalloid resuscitation begun. Hemoglobin on arrival 7.4. Urgent upper endoscopy found an actively bleeding gastric ulcer and he was taken to the OR for operative repair of the ulcer, with biopsy of its edge.

Intraoperatively he was given packed red cells. Shortly after the second unit was hung he developed rigors, dyspnea and flank pain, his pressure fell further and he became agitated and tachycardic. The transfusion was stopped at once and the reaction protocol followed. The bag returned to the blood bank for investigation. Over the following hours the urinary catheter drained dark, red-brown urine and his sclerae turned yellow. Labs on 05/08: creatinine up from 1.08 on arrival to 2.36, indirect bilirubin 3.4, plasma free hemoglobin 85, direct antiglobulin test positive, schistocytes on the peripheral smear. Diagnosis: acute hemolytic transfusion reaction.

He was monitored in the surgical ICU with fluids and supportive care, urine output followed hourly. No further transfusion. Pressures stabilized, urine cleared over 48 hours, creatinine trended down (1.42 on the day of discharge). Hemoglobin 9.1 at discharge without further products. Lisinopril held through the hypotension and the kidney injury, resumed on 05/12. Tolerating a regular diet, incision clean.

Pathology: benign gastric ulcer, no malignancy, H. pylori negative.

ALLERGY ADDED: BLOOD PRODUCTS — acute hemolytic transfusion reaction. Any future transfusion only after blood bank consultation.

Discharge medications: pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily (new); lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Avoid NSAIDs.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC and BMP; general surgery clinic in 2 weeks; GI for repeat endoscopy in 8 to 10 weeks to confirm healing.

Tobacco: strongly advised to stop; impairs ulcer healing.

Signed: general surgery attending.

documents.title: Hospital records received

documents.body: Discharge summary and path report received from the hospital, filed. Flagged to PCP: new allergy to blood products. Allergy list updated. TCM call to RN pool.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge outreach, day 1 home. Pt says he is tired, sore at the incision, eating small meals. No vomiting, no black stools, urine looks normal color now. Has pantoprazole and is taking it twice a day. Reviewed: no ibuprofen or naproxen, acetaminophen ok for pain. Reminded him his allergy list now includes blood products and to say so at any hospital. Visit booked 5/21 with labs that morning.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 8 days after discharge from the surgical service (admitted 5/7 to 5/13). Discharge summary reviewed in full.

What happened: vomited blood, bleeding gastric ulcer found on scope, operated on the same morning. Got a transfusion in the OR and had an acute hemolytic reaction: hypotension, dark urine, jaundice, a bump in creatinine to 2.36, DAT positive. ICU, then the floor. Path benign, H. pylori negative.

Now: energy coming back slowly. Walking the yard. Incision sore but closed. Eating normally. Stools brown. No lightheadedness. Urine normal color. Taking pantoprazole twice daily, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Not back at work yet. Smoking again since he got home, less than before, he says.

Exam: pale-ish but better. No scleral icterus. Midline upper abdominal incision healing well, no drainage. Heart regular, lungs clear.

Labs today: Hgb 10.6 (9.1 at discharge). Cr 1.02, back to his usual. T bili 0.9.

A/P
1. Bleeding gastric ulcer s/p repair: PPI twice daily until GI rescope. Surgery clinic next week. No NSAIDs, ever, is the simple rule.
2. Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction: resolved. Kidney function and bilirubin normal. Allergy to blood products on our list with the details; he knows to bring it up.
3. Anemia from the bleed: recovering without iron need for now; CBC at physical.
4. Tobacco: smoking again. Told him the ulcer and the heart both argue for stopping now. Declines a patch or pills; says he will try on his own.
5. HTN: a little high today, sore and a long week; lisinopril back on since 5/12. Recheck at physical.

RTC at physical in Sept.

documents.title: General Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Allard in clinic on 05/28/2024, three weeks after operative repair of a bleeding gastric ulcer. He is eating well and his pain is minimal. The incision is healing cleanly with no sign of infection or hernia. He may return to light duties now and full lifting after six weeks from surgery. He has a GI appointment for repeat endoscopy. Please note his allergy to blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction). No further surgical follow-up is needed unless problems arise.

Regards,
General surgery

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY — ESOPHAGOGASTRODUODENOSCOPY
Indication: follow-up of bleeding gastric ulcer repaired surgically 05/2024; confirm healing.
Allergies: blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: normal esophagus and GE junction. Stomach: healed ulcer scar with surrounding postsurgical change; no active ulceration, no visible vessel. Biopsies taken from the scar. Duodenum normal to the second portion.
Impression: healed gastric ulcer.
Plan: reduce pantoprazole to 40 mg once daily and continue long term given the history. Avoid NSAIDs. Smoking cessation advised. Will forward biopsy results.

Addendum 07/19: biopsies benign, no H. pylori.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 06:50 by private vehicle (driven by a coworker).

CC: chest pain.

HPI: 55M, coronary disease, admitted last year for an upper GI bleed. Woke around 04:45 with a severe crushing pain mid-chest going down the left arm, now 2 hours. Short of breath, nauseated, drenched in sweat. Took nothing for it.

PMH (per our system): HTN, hyperlipidemia, CAD, peptic ulcer disease, tobacco use disorder, acute hemolytic transfusion reaction 2024.
PSH: operative repair of bleeding gastric ulcer.
Meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Allergies: BLOOD PRODUCTS (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).
FH: CAD.
SH: smokes 1 pack per day.

VS: BP 150/90, HR 98, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA.
Exam: diaphoretic, uncomfortable. Heart regular, no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Lungs clear. No JVD. Extremities warm.

ECG at 06:54: ST elevation II, III, aVF. STEMI alert called, interventional cardiology paged.
Troponin I 0.5 ng/mL (ref <0.04). CK-MB 25 U/L (ref 0-24). CBC and BMP within normal limits.
Portable CXR: unremarkable.

Assessment: inferior STEMI.
ED course: STEMI pathway, prior GI bleed flagged to the interventional team; to cath lab 07:40.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/22/2025, discharged 04/25/2025.

Diagnosis: acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Procedure: emergent coronary angiography and PCI. Culprit: total occlusion of the right coronary artery, treated with one drug-eluting stent with TIMI 3 flow restored. Right radial access.

Course: uncomplicated after PCI. No recurrent pain, no arrhythmia on telemetry. Echo 04/23: LVEF 55%, inferior hypokinesis, no significant valve disease. Given his 2024 bleeding gastric ulcer, clopidogrel chosen as the P2Y12 agent and pantoprazole continued.

Allergies: blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).

Discharge medications:
- aspirin 81 mg daily (new)
- clopidogrel 75 mg daily (new), do not stop without talking to cardiology; planned 12 months
- metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (new)
- atorvastatin 80 mg daily (increased from 40)
- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed (new)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (continued)
- pantoprazole 40 mg daily (continued)

Smoking: counseled at length; declined pharmacotherapy.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; cardiology clinic 4 weeks; cardiac rehab referral sent. No driving for 1 week, no heavy lifting for 1 week from the radial site.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One week out from an inferior STEMI (4/22), RCA occlusion stented, home 4/25. Discharge summary and echo reviewed: EF 55%, inferior hypokinesis.

He is shaken. No chest pain since the cath. Wrist site a little bruised. Walking the driveway and back without trouble. No black stools on aspirin plus clopidogrel. Mild fatigue, he thinks from the metoprolol. Has not used the nitro.

Med rec done with bottles: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole 40, nitro SL prn. All filled.

Smoking: says he has cut way back, then admits to about a pack a day again by the weekend.

PHQ-9: 3.

Exam: BP and HR as charted. R radial site with small ecchymosis, good pulse, no hematoma. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p DES to RCA: DAPT x 12 months, keep the PPI with it given the ulcer. Reviewed bleeding signs to call about. Reviewed nitro use and when to call 911.
2. CAD: high-intensity statin now. Lipids in 3 months.
3. HTN: better on the added metoprolol.
4. Tobacco: the single most important thing now. Offered varenicline again; he declines, wants to try cold turkey. Quitline info.
5. Cardiac rehab: referral in; he is calling them this week.
6. BMP today on the new regimen.

RTC 3 months.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sharing the care of Kevin Allard, seen today 4 weeks after an inferior STEMI treated with a drug-eluting stent to the right coronary artery.

He has had no angina and has not needed nitroglycerin. He started cardiac rehabilitation last week. No bleeding on dual antiplatelet therapy. He continues to smoke.

Blood pressure and heart rate at goal. Regular rhythm, clear lungs, radial site healed.

Impression: CAD s/p PCI to RCA, LVEF 55%, clinically stable.
Plan: continue aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75 for 12 months, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole 40. Smoking cessation urged. Return in 6 months.

Allergies: blood products.

Sincerely,
Outside cardiology

Allergies: BLOOD PRODUCTS.
FH: father MI at 62, mother HTN, brother hyperlipidemia.
SH: 30 pack-year smoker.

VS: BP 150/90, HR 98, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air.
Exam: diaphoretic, anxious. Cardiac regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear to auscultation.

ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF.
Labs: troponin I 0.5 ng/mL (ref <0.04); CK-MB 25 U/L (ref 0-24); CBC and electrolytes normal.
CXR: unremarkable.

Impression: recurrent inferior STEMI.
Plan: STEMI activation; to cath lab 16:05; cardiology admitting.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/23/2025, discharged 10/25/2025.

Diagnosis: recurrent acute inferior STEMI.
Procedure: emergent coronary angiography: new severe stenosis of the proximal right coronary artery; the April 2025 RCA stent widely patent. One drug-eluting stent to the proximal RCA, TIMI 3 flow. Right radial access.

Course: pain-free after PCI, telemetry without arrhythmia, radial site clean. Patient confirms taking aspirin and clopidogrel daily.

Allergies: blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).

Discharge medications (unchanged from admission):
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- clopidogrel 75 mg daily; dual antiplatelet therapy now planned through 10/2026
- metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily
- atorvastatin 80 mg daily
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- pantoprazole 40 mg daily
- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL prn

Smoking cessation counseling repeated; declined medication.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; cardiology 6 weeks.

documents.title: Hospital records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ED record and cardiology discharge summary received, filed. No med changes. Post-hospital visit booked 10/30.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Second inferior STEMI on 10/23, six months after the first. Cath: new tight lesion in the proximal RCA, the April stent open. Another DES. Home 10/25, no med changes, DAPT clock reset to October 2026.

He is quieter than usual today. Says the crew saw the whole thing. No chest pain since, no nitro, no bleeding. Taking everything, showed me the weekly pill box.

PHQ-9 4, not depressed, worried.

Exam: right wrist healing. Regular rhythm, clear lungs, no edema.

A/P
1. Recurrent inferior STEMI s/p second RCA stent. Meds unchanged per cardiology: aspirin, clopidogrel through 10/2026, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole 40, NTG prn.
2. Tobacco: told him plainly that the cigarettes are the one risk still fully in his hands. Offered varenicline or patch plus gum. Declines; says he will cut down for the winter.
3. Return to work: cardiology's call; he will ask at the 6-week visit.

RTC January.

documents.title: Cardiology Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Kevin Allard returns 6 weeks after a second inferior STEMI with a drug-eluting stent to the proximal right coronary artery. He has been free of angina and has not taken nitroglycerin. No bleeding on dual antiplatelet therapy. Still smoking, somewhat less.

Blood pressure and heart rate at goal, rhythm regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

Plan: no changes. Aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg through October 2026, then reassess. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg. May return to full work duties. Smoking cessation strongly advised. Return in 5 to 6 months.

Sincerely,
Outside cardiology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 months after the second MI.

Back to full duty per cardiology, which in January means the plow truck and the shop. No angina. No nitro. Some easy bruising on the forearms from the two antiplatelets, no other bleeding. Stools normal.

Smoking: says about half a pack on work days, more on weekends. Honest that it has crept back up.

Meds unchanged: ASA 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole 40, NTG prn.
Allergy: blood products (AHTR 2024).

Exam: well. Regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Forearm bruises, scattered, small. No edema.

A/P
- CAD, old inferior MI x2, RCA stents x2: stable. Closed the acute STEMI entry; old MI and stent status remain. DAPT through October.
- Lipids/LFT/CBC today.
- HTN: at goal.
- Tobacco: counseled again; he will not take a medication. Left the door open.

RTC 3 months, can be video.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I need the pantoprazole and the metoprolol sent again, the pharmacy says no refills left. Same pharmacy. Thanks, Kevin

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Kevin, both sent this morning with refills through the year. They should be ready this afternoon.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he is in his truck on his lunch break, parked. Consent and identity confirmed.

Spring cleanups started. No chest pressure on the job, no shortness of breath beyond baseline, no lightheadedness. No bleeding. Taking all meds, the pill box is in the glovebox. Home BP readings he reads off his phone are in a good range.

Smoking about the same.

A/P: CAD s/p 2 RCA stents, stable. HTN controlled at home. No changes. Cardiology visit next month. In-person visit with labs in July.
Tobacco: brief counseling.

documents.title: Cardiology Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Routine follow-up for Kevin Allard: CAD with drug-eluting stents to the RCA in April and October 2025 after inferior STEMIs, LVEF 55%.

No angina, no nitroglycerin use, working full duty as a landscaping supervisor. Minor bruising only on dual antiplatelet therapy. Continues to smoke.

Examination unremarkable; blood pressure and heart rate at goal.

Plan: continue aspirin and clopidogrel through October 2026, then we will decide on single antiplatelet therapy. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg. Smoking cessation again urged. Return in 6 months.

Allergies: blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).

Sincerely,
Outside cardiology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mid-summer check, labs drawn before the visit.

Heat has been rough on the crews; he is keeping himself to supervising and running the mower less. No chest discomfort with exertion, no nitro since he got the bottle. No palpitations, no syncope. Bruises easily, no other bleeding. Stomach quiet.

Still smoking. Asked him what would make the difference; he says maybe when the DAPT ends and he 'feels like a normal person again,' which I pointed out is backwards. He laughed.

Meds reviewed, unchanged. Allergy: blood products.

Exam: tan, comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Legs without edema, pedal pulses present.

A/P
1. CAD with old inferior MIs and RCA stents x2: stable on aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril, NTG prn. Clopidogrel end date is cardiology's call in October.
2. HTN: controlled.
3. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today.
4. Gastric ulcer hx: pantoprazole daily.
5. Tobacco use disorder: counseled; declines pharmacotherapy.
6. Health maintenance: LDCT due October, flu and COVID in the fall.

RTC October.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kevin, labs from Wednesday look good: kidney and liver tests normal on the atorvastatin, blood count normal on the two blood thinners, and your LDL is holding where we want it. No changes. See you in October.
